title: Customer network change storyboard and audit evidence patterns
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working sketch for a more compact, customer-friendly approach to capturing forensic evidence for VPC/network changes in Private Deployments. Goal: make approval gates lightweight for customers while preserving a forensically useful audit trail for compliance and incident investigation. This is intentionally a pragmatic draft — lots of open questions listed at the end.

High-level idea
- Capture a minimal "change storyboard" for each customer-initiated network change. The storyboard is an ordered set of discrete events (request, pre-checks, approval decision(s), apply, post-checks, snapshot evidence) that together tell the narrative of what happened.
- Store a compact evidence envelope per storyboard that contains pointers to artifacts (logs, signed assertions, snapshots) plus a small inline provenance summary so that the audit view loads quickly.
- Allow two sampling modes: full-capture (for high-risk changes or customers requiring detailed logs) and compact-sampling (default) that captures required attestations + selective telemetry.

Why different from existing flows
- Existing proposals tend to prefer either huge full logs (heavy on storage/transfer) or simple acceptance receipts. This balances both: keep the canonical story but limit heavy artifacts to on-demand retrieval.

Storyboard model (conceptual)
- event: request.submitted 
  - who: identifier of requesting principal (customer-admin or operator)
  - when: timestamp
  - intent: free-text + normalized op_type (e.g., route-add, firewall-change, peering)
  - ticket: optional linked ticket id
- event: automated.preflight
  - result: pass|warn|fail
  - checks-run: list of check ids
- event: approval.flow
  - approvers: list of approver identities (could be customer OAuth principals or operator service accounts)
  - decision: approve|reject|escalate
  - evidence_ref: id of evidence envelope or URL shortlink
- event: apply.start
  - plan_digest: short hash of intended changes (deterministic canonical form)
- event: apply.complete
  - result_summary: success|partial|failed
  - duration_ms: integer
- event: post-validate
  - probe_summary: quick probes run and results
- event: snapshot
  - snapshot_ref: object with minimal inline metadata (size, retention tier, blob id)

Compact evidence envelope (inline summary + pointers)
- envelope_id: short uuid
- created_by: service or principal
- created_ts: timestamp
- summary: 1-2 sentences describing the change (human-readable)
- provenance_digest: short digest over the canonical storyboard and key artifacts (allows quick tamper detection)
- pointers: list of artifacts (each: {type,label,short_uri})  <-- presented here as prose in the doc, actual implementation is a compact list in the DB
- inline_assertions: list of short signed assertions (example: "preflight-checks-passed:v1", "approver-1-signature")
- retention_tier: hot|warm|cold (controls retention and retrieval cost)

Note: the envelope intentionally does not contain raw packet captures or full debug logs; those are stored as external blobs referenced by pointers and retrieved on demand.

Sampling policy (defaults + customer overrides)
- default (compact): all storyboard events recorded; envelope created; only 1-minute sampled telemetry for performance baselines; heavy artifacts retained for 7 days then archived to cold tier (customer can request retrieval).
- high-fidelity (customer opt-in or policy): full telemetry + full logs + snapshots for 90 days; recommended for PCI-like customers.
- risk-triggered: if preflight fails or automated anomaly detection flags the change, escalate to full-capture automatically and notify security + customer admin.

Approval gate UX and automation
- Gate presets: low-risk (auto-approve), medium (single approver + timebox), high (2-of-3 approvers or scheduled window).
- UI: succinct inline story view — top of page shows short summary, current gate status, who approved, and a small "forensics snapshot" section that displays the envelope summary (no heavy blobs unless user clicks).
- API: approvals endpoint should return envelope id and minimal verification tokens so downstream systems (SIEMs) can ingest a single line of truth without fetching full artifacts.
- Audit CSV export: generate a compact CSV row per storyboard with columns: envelope_id, change_type, initiator, approvers_comma, decision, plan_digest, created_ts, retention_tier, artifact_count. This helps security teams ingest into existing BI/archival tools.

Evidence retention and legal considerations
- Minimum default retention for compact envelopes: 365 days metadata + 90 days for heavy artifacts in hot/warm depending on tier.
- Provide a "legal hold" flag at the envelope level controlled by customer or Redwood legal to prevent deletion.
- Data residency: envelopes and pointers must respect customer-selected region; heavy artifacts may be cross-region only with explicit consent.

APIs and schema notes (implementation sketch)
- /v1/private/vpcs/{vpc_id}/change-storyboards POST body: a minimal canonical change representation + optional ticket link. Returns storyboard_id and envelope_id.
- /v1/envelopes/{envelope_id} GET: returns envelope summary and signed provenance token. Full artifact list included as short URIs. Retrieval of heavy blobs happens via a signed short-lived URL.
- Signed assertions format: base64(signed-compact-assertion) with signer id and algorithm metadata appended. Keep assertion size small to enable inline storage.

Operational considerations
- Storage cost modeling: assume default compact envelope is ~1–3KB of inline metadata; heavy artifacts average 2–20MB per change when full-capture. Need to model per-customer expected CR changes per month to propose pricing tiers.
- RBAC: envelope metadata may be visible to operator and customer admins; heavy artifacts only to allowed roles (customer security admins, Redwood incident responders with customer consent).
- Retrieval flow: require an audit log entry when a heavy artifact is accessed. That access itself becomes part of the storyboard (evidence_accessed event).

Open questions / next steps
- What exactly belongs in inline_assertions vs external blobs? Define a minimal set of signed assertions required for regulatory audits.
- Decide default retention tiers and their costs with finance.
- UX work: mock quick-view card for the Console and a compact CSV export example.
- API security: recommended signing algorithm and token rotation cadence for signed assertions.
- Compliance catalog: map this model to SOC2/ISO requirements and produce a one-pager for Sales.

Action items (owners)
- Draft canonical assertion list (Priya Nair) — due 2025-02-05
- Cost model for storage + retrieval (Diego Ruiz) — due 2025-02-12
- Console quick-view mock (Ethan Chen) — due 2025-02-14
- Security review of signing approach (Maya Thompson & eng-sec) — due 2025-02-21

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Keep envelope small and indexable — the whole point is fast queries for legal/compliance.
- Make it trivial for customers to bump to full-capture for a specific ticket/change without changing org-level policy.
- Consider a lightweight Kafka topic for storyboards so partner SIEMs can subscribe to near-real-time change events without pulling blobs.

Example compact envelope (as an inline human-readable snippet)
- envelope_id: env_8f3c2a
- created_by: service:private-deployments
- created_ts: 2025-01-07T15:33:12Z
- summary: "Add route for partner-x to cross-account peering"
- provenance_digest: sha256:6b3c...
- pointers: [ preflight_report: s3://rwd-prod/envelopes/8f3c2a/preflight.pdf (hot), config_plan: s3://rwd-prod/plans/plan_a1 (cold) ]
- inline_assertions: [ "preflight:pass:v1:sig_by_service", "approver:alice@example.com:sig" ]
- retention_tier: warm

If you skim and want to iterate: prioritize defining the minimal signed assertions and the CSV export schema next. This doc is intentionally a lightweight narrative + operational checklist rather than another full-blown PRD.
plain_text_summary: Working draft: minimal change storyboard + compact evidence envelope for customer-managed network changes. Balances quick auditability with reduced heavy artifact storage. Defines storyboard events, envelope fields, sampling policies, approval gate UX, API sketches, retention rules, and action items.
